content:
If you're like me, you've probably spent hours clicking around on Wikipedia, randomly browsing articles. Now there's finally an official app—and honestly, it's more of a little tool—to let you do exactly that.

Now there's finally a button that can take you directly to a random Wikipedia article.

The Wikipedia iOS app's update today added a fun and practical new feature: a "Random Article" widget that can be placed on your iPhone or iPad home screen.

The widget comes in both large and medium sizes, and features a cute mascot.

Tap the widget once and it will take you to a completely random Wikipedia article, opening it in random mode.

No need to leave the app and tap the widget again—just hit the random button and you can keep rolling the dice, diving deeper and deeper into this random maze.

Have fun, but be careful not to lose track of time. Earlier this summer, the Wikipedia app also added a history trivia mini-game.

After you update the Wikipedia iPhone and iPad apps today, you'll be able to find this brand-new widget.

Enjoy your Apple device to the fullest!
